title: Santa Cruz Otter Steals Surfboard: Viral Video
text:
Santa Cruz Otter Incident: Surfer’s Board Stolen, Echoes of ‘Otter 841’
A mischievous otter snatched a surfboard from a surfer at Steamer lane in Santa Cruz, California, on Wednesday, prompting a response from emergency services. The incident bears a striking resemblance to the well-documented antics of a notorious local sea otter known as “Otter 841,” who gained fame in the summer of 2023 for similar board thefts adn even wave-riding.
According to a statement released by the Santa Cruz Fire Department Marine Division, emergency responders were dispatched around 5:06 p.m. following a report that a surfer may have been bitten. Though, officials quickly persistent that the surfer was unharmed.
Lifeguards arriving at the scene found a group of surfers surrounding another in the water, with “an otter who appeared to be sitting on the victim’s board,” the fire department reported. The surfer was brought ashore and assessed by medical personnel, confirming no injuries had occurred.
“Lifeguards retrieved and returned the board to the surfer,” a department spokesperson stated. “Once the equipment was given back to the owner, units were cleared from the incident.”
The incident unfolded when a surfer at Steamer Lane had their board taken by an otter. The surfer reported a possible bite, triggering a dispatch to the Santa Cruz Fire department Marine Division. Upon arrival, lifeguards discovered the otter comfortably positioned on the stolen board. The surfer was evaluated and found to be uninjured, and the board was safely returned.
While the recent incident evokes memories of Otter 841, the fire department confirmed that the otter involved in Wednesday’s event has not been identified as the same individual. Otter 841 was eventually relocated to a facility in Monterey Bay after repeated encounters with humans.
The city of Santa Cruz plans to inform the California Department of Fish and wildlife about the latest incident. This proactive step underscores the growing concern regarding interactions between wildlife and the public in the area.
Authorities will continue to monitor the situation and work to ensure the safety of both surfers and the local otter population. The california Department of Fish and Wildlife will be consulted to determine if further action is needed to address the increasing frequency of these otter-surfer encounters.
